title: pvHistogram2D
body:
## pvHistogram2D

Builds a joint (2-D) histogram of two array components and outputs it as a 2-D image (vtkImageData) whose point scalars are the counts: X-variable bins along the image x axis, Y bins along y. By ParaView default the Y variable is the gradient magnitude of the X array, the value-versus-gradient plot used to design volume-rendering transfer functions; turn UseGradientasYAxisArray off to histogram two arbitrary arrays, e.g. temperature against pressure. Both arrays must have the same association and number of tuples. Use pvHistogram for one variable.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Origin and spacing only place the image; binning always spans the arrays' finite ranges or the custom ranges. With the defaults (origin [0, 0], spacing [1, 1]) image coordinates are bin indices; enable HistogramBoundsfromInput to read the axes in data units.
- While UseGradientasYAxisArray is true (the native default), InputArrayforYAxis and the Y custom range are ignored.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `Histogram2D`. Identity: `filters/ExtractHistogram2D`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Histogram filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). The input needs at least one point- or cell-centred array. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ComponentforXAxisarray` | The value of this property specifies the array component from which the histogram should be computed. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ComponentforYAxisarray` | The value of this property specifies the array component from which the histogram should be computed. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `CustomBinRangesforXAxis` | Set custom bin ranges to use. These are used only when UseCustomBinRanges is set to true. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1]` |
| `CustomBinRangesforYAxis` | Set custom bin ranges to use. These are used only when UseCustomBinRanges is set to true. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1]` |
| `HistogramBoundsfromInput` | When set to true, the input scalar ranges will be used to compute the histogram origin and spacing. By default, set to false. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `HistogramOrigin` | The origin of the output histogram image. These are used only when UseInputRangesForOutputBounds is set to false. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1]` |
| `HistogramSpacing` | The pixel spacing of the output histogram image. These are used only when UseInputRangesForOutputBounds is set to false. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1]` |
| `InputArrayforXAxis` | This property indicates the name of the array from which to compute the histogram. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `InputArrayforYAxis` | This property indicates the name of the array from which to compute the histogram. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `NumberofBins` | Number of bins along each axis as [X bins, Y bins]; these are also the output image dimensions in pixels. Each variable's range is divided among its bins, so more bins resolve finer structure but leave fewer samples per bin and noisier counts. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1]` |
| `UseCustomBinRangesforXAxis` | When set to true, custom bin ranges will be used instead of using the full range for the selected array for X axis. By default, set to false. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `UseCustomBinRangesforYAxis` | When set to true, custom bin ranges will be used instead of using the full range for the selected array for X axis. By default, set to false. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `UseGradientasYAxisArray` | If this property is on, the gradient of the input scalar array will be used for the Y axis of the 2D histogram. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
